nodes.label: Trip Kailash Design Package
nodes.rationale: The single creative deliverable: every redesign decision lives in one file so a builder needs nothing else. Every build phase consumes it.

nodes.label: Two Governing Rules: copy verbatim, numbers provisional
nodes.rationale: Copy ships verbatim because the doc is where writing happens and templates are only wiring, so paraphrase in a build pass is drift. Band ranges and pacing numbers are labelled starting points because only the flick test against real footage can validate them.

nodes.label: Section 0: The Research
nodes.rationale: Research precedes design per the method: find the exact language buyers use about pains, desires and hesitations, then write the site in those words rather than in the operator's words.

nodes.label: The Fire Horse Year Finding
nodes.rationale: 2026 is the Tibetan Fire Horse Year: a Horse Year comes every twelve, a Fire Horse Year every sixty, and a kora walked in one is held to carry the merit of thirteen. Next Horse Year 2038, next Fire Horse Year 2086. The current site never mentioned it, which is the single largest missed positioning asset.

nodes.label: The Urgent Position (time-boxed band)
nodes.rationale: Runs only if a September departure can genuinely be permitted; comes down on 1 October and is never faked, because an urgency banner outliving its deadline tells returning visitors nothing on the site is maintained.

nodes.label: The Durable Position: 2027 is the better year
nodes.rationale: Every competitor is selling the hype year, so almost nobody will say the honest thing afterwards: 2027 is quiet, permits come easier, lodges are not full, guides look after eight people not thirty. Competitors cannot copy it without contradicting their own 2026 marketing, and it turns the brief's weakest asset into an advantage.

nodes.label: Pain: fear of being defrauded
nodes.rationale: The number one objection and not paranoia: a Hyderabad operator took over Rs 15 lakh from seven Bengaluru pilgrims and never ran the trip; sponsored emails fake operator credentials.

nodes.label: Pain: money vanishing into permits
nodes.rationale: 20-30% deposits are standard and commonly non-refundable; once a Tibet permit is applied for no refund exists. Buyers are braced for vagueness, so plainness here is the differentiator.

nodes.label: Pain: altitude, badly handled
nodes.rationale: About 35% fall ill if flown straight to Mansarovar at 4,550 m; skipping acclimatisation is why pilgrims are turned back below Dolma La. The sharpest research line: pilgrims prepare the spiritual side for months and treat altitude as an afterthought.

nodes.label: Pain: booking for elderly parents
nodes.rationale: A large share of buyers are adult children booking for a parent. Their language is duty and dignity, not adventure, and they fear the road journey more than the shrine.

nodes.label: The Desire: a journey inward, never a trek
nodes.rationale: Buyers say burn away, inner journey, felt the presence, transformation, sins. Selling Kailash as a trek is the wrong frame for the person actually buying, and every competitor does it.

nodes.label: The Testimonial Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Pilgrims consistently want to tell people afterwards. Asking at the right moment (post-trip email plus a photo-permission checkbox in the booking form) closes the site's biggest weakness, which is having no reviews.

nodes.label: Invite Verification, Do Not Display Numbers
nodes.rationale: Buyer guidance says a properly registered agency actively encourages verification. TAAN and NTB registers are public, so handing over the means to check costs nothing, is impossible to fake, answers the category's number one objection, and no competitor does it. It becomes a named section, not a footer line.

nodes.label: The One Call To Action: the enquiry
nodes.rationale: The business closes by enquiry, confirmation, invoice, then a 30% deposit. The site never pretends to be a checkout because a checkout button leading to an enquiry form is a small lie at the worst moment.

nodes.label: Tier 1: The Single Journey
nodes.rationale: One 6-second shot scrubbed by scroll, captions in the negative space, page settling at the composed ending. Chosen because a single clip already exists and the boldness budget is spent on the pinned parikrama gallery and kora ring instead of a chained hero. Tier 2 chaining is a free later upgrade.

nodes.label: The Creative Director's Loop (seven hats)
nodes.rationale: Producer, Researcher, Storyboarder, Prompt generator, Designer, Website producer, Gatekeeper. Gates run in order: package approved, footage validated against the twelve laws, build self-tested, copy gate, then live verification with speed receipts.

nodes.label: Producer's Mobile Decision: phones get the designed still
nodes.rationale: Most traffic is Indian and Nepali mobile where the video is never worth its weight. If no usable clip exists at all the hero becomes a composed still and the pinned gallery carries the signature alone, costing one section and no rework.

nodes.label: The Brand Premise: Parikrama
nodes.rationale: You do not climb what is sacred, you walk around it. Trekking companies sell the top; Trip Kailash sells the circle. Confirmed by research: the circle is the unit of merit, a Horse Year multiplies koras not summits. It also solves the commercial problem, making Kailash the thing the catalogue is measured against rather than a $2,500 ask from a stranger. Kailash sits last in every sequence because you arrive at the mountain.

nodes.label: The Palette as CSS Tokens
nodes.rationale: Three families carry the site: sandalwood for surfaces (--sand-50 #FBF6EC to --sand-300 #DCCAA9), brass for structure and ornament (--brass-300 #E0C489 to --brass-600 #8A6408), vermilion reserved for one job (--verm-500 #A8452C), with bark as the ink (--bark-900 #1E1006 to --bark-300 #A9906B) and a warm night ground (--night-900 #0E0904) for cinematic sections.

nodes.label: Rule: vermilion is rationed
nodes.rationale: It appears on booking actions and nowhere else. Sindoor is a mark applied to one spot, not a wash; on eleven things per page it stops meaning act here.

nodes.label: Rule: no drop shadows
nodes.rationale: Depth comes from three steps of sandalwood plus hairline borders. Shadows on a warm palette turn muddy and are the visual tell of a page-builder site.

nodes.label: Rule: small radii, one drawn curve
nodes.rationale: Temple architecture is cut stone, not soft plastic: --r 4px generally, --rlg 10px for cards. The system's only curve is the torana arch, and it is drawn rather than rounded.

nodes.label: Rule: never pure black or pure white
nodes.rationale: Sand at the top of the ramp, warm near-black at the bottom, keeping the whole ramp inside one warm family.

nodes.label: Rule: sandalwood is also the practical choice
nodes.rationale: Photography is a mix with gaps; muted warm backgrounds hide inconsistent white balance where a bright white page exposes every bad frame.

nodes.label: Grading Tokens (colour paired with the word)
nodes.rationale: --grade-easy #5C7A3F, --grade-moderate #B8860B, --grade-hard #A8452C. Colour always travels with the word because a coloured dot alone tells a colour-blind reader nothing, and grading is the field a buyer uses to decide whether they can go.

nodes.label: The Type Trio: Cinzel, Karla, Noto Serif Devanagari
nodes.rationale: Cinzel (700/900) is Trajan-column inscriptional lettering, carved rather than printed, which is where the monumental feeling comes from; it renders as capitals so it is restricted to headings, buttons and labels. Karla (400/500) carries body prose. Noto Serif Devanagari (500/700) is first-class, not a fallback, because rendering terms like Dasa-Divasiya Siva-Parikrama in a system fallback reads as carelessness about the tradition.

nodes.label: Deviation: no mono, Cinzel small labels plus tabular-nums
nodes.rationale: The 10k standard asks for a mono for small labels, but a mono reads techy against temple stone. Cinzel at 12px with 0.22em tracking is the brand's small-label voice, and numeric readouts get font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on Karla. Three faces not four also matters on this audience's connections.

nodes.label: Self-host all three faces
nodes.rationale: woff2 only, trimmed to the exact weights, font-display: swap, no request to fonts.googleapis.com. The DNS lookup and round trip cost real seconds on Indian and Nepali mobile.

nodes.label: The Band Map (hero scroll choreography)
nodes.rationale: The hero is sized in scroll distance rather than seconds: roughly 400vh for one 6-second shot, so pacing is independent of clip length and a shorter trim costs nothing.

nodes.label: Band 1: Some mountains are climbed
nodes.rationale: 0.00-0.16 over the cold wide. Word-by-word rise, opened settled by a one-time load ramp so the hero never sits wordless at scroll zero.

nodes.label: Band 2: Fifty-two kilometres, one circle
nodes.rationale: 0.20-0.42 as the camera travels the trail. Drift-down entrance: the words fall into place as the prayer flags fall.

nodes.label: Band 3: the merit multiplier
nodes.rationale: Changed after the research: it used to be a pleasant line about the people we walk with that said nothing. The Horse Year multiplier is the single fact that reframes the decision, and it belongs at the moment the footage reaches the pass. Blur-to-sharp entrance echoes the haze clearing. Must be verified before shipping because sources split between thirteen and twelve.

nodes.label: Band 4: the settle
nodes.rationale: 0.74-1.00 on the composed resting frame: headline, then subline at --k 0.66, then the CTA row at 0.78. Three arrivals in one band. The ghost action changed from 'Kailash 2027' (a date) to 'Kailash, and which year to walk it', which is the question the high-intent visitor is actually carrying.

nodes.label: The Flick Test
nodes.rationale: Band ranges are starting points validated at 120, 240 and 360px wheel steps against the real footage; the ranges move if the test says so.

nodes.label: Four-Layer Legibility System
nodes.rationale: Global base scrim, per-band radial scrim riding that band's --k, a three-layer text shadow token, and chip backings on small labels over footage. Tuned against each band's own worst frame, never the average, and every band must clear 3.5:1 worst-pixel contrast before anyone sees the page. Buttons never carry the shadow because a shadowed label reads as grime.

nodes.label: The Static-Hero Copy Block
nodes.rationale: Phones, portrait tablets, coarse-pointer portrait, landscape phones and reduced motion get a designed layout over the ending frame, not a fallback apology, and neither the video nor its poster is requested on that path.

nodes.label: The Five Static-Hero Gates
nodes.rationale: Five media queries matched character for character between CSS and the JS decision, and kept live with change listeners so a rotating tablet or a mid-session reduced-motion flip re-arms correctly.

nodes.label: The Below-Fold Outline (nine sections)
nodes.rationale: No two adjacent sections share a layout skeleton, and every section funnels to the single enquiry. If a section does not serve the parikrama premise it does not belong on the page.

nodes.label: 6.1 Hero
nodes.rationale: Settles into the approved headline and the two actions.

nodes.label: 6.2 Choose Your Path
nodes.rationale: Three doors (Shaiva, Buddhist, Vaishnava) placed above the packages deliberately: it reframes what the visitor thinks they are shopping for before they see a price, because once someone is comparing $350 to $1,000 the pilgrimage framing is gone and you compete on cost with all of Thamel. Counts are computed live from the Tradition taxonomy and never typed; Tradition is multi-select so counts do not sum to the package total.

nodes.label: Door Geometries: torana, dharma wheel, shaligram facet
nodes.rationale: One drawn geometry per door, never one icon recoloured; each draws its stroke on scroll in reading order with a 90ms stagger between outer and inner figure.

nodes.label: 6.3 The Parikrama (signature pinned gallery)
nodes.rationale: Night ground, pinned horizontal scroll, faded in and out through the sand by gradient masks so it never reads as a stripe. Order is fixed Muktinath, Gosaikunda, Maratika, Shiva Divine, Kailash last, because you arrive at the mountain. Copy describes sacred meaning and never logistics, since every competitor leads with logistics. Falloff is continuous rather than a hard toggle (blur 0-4.5px, opacity 1-0.4, scale 1-0.86); below 900px pinning is switched off for a native swipe because pinned scroll-jacking on phones is reliably awful and most traffic is phones.

nodes.label: 6.4 Which Year To Walk It
nodes.rationale: Rebuilt from the research and now the commercial centre of the homepage. Left column carries the durable 2027 position, right column carries Nepal yatras on the visitor's own dates, and the time-boxed Fire Horse band sits above both only while a departure can genuinely run.

nodes.label: The Kora Ring (the one interactive moment)
nodes.rationale: One interaction per site, on theme, performed mid-journey: a brass ring the visitor holds and turns while an altitude readout climbs the real Kailash kora profile (Darchen 4,675 m, Dirapuk 4,910 m, Dolma La 5,630 m, Zutulpuk 4,790 m, Darchen closed). The payoff changed after the research from revealing dates to revealing the merit multiplier, so the visitor learns the decisive fact by performing the thing it describes. Releasing early eases progress back rather than snapping to zero; reduced motion gets the completed state with no hold required.

nodes.label: 6.5 Check Us Before You Pay Us
nodes.rationale: A new section and the highest-value thing the research produced. It names the fear out loud, then hands over TAAN, NTB, company registration, the parent company and a real office address with the places to check each. The closing line, that if anything does not check out you should not travel with us, is the whole section in one sentence and no competitor will copy it.

nodes.label: 6.6 How a Place is Confirmed
nodes.rationale: Three numbered steps (enquire, confirm and invoice, pay 30%), placed before the lineage section on purpose: for an international wire transfer to Nepal, uncertainty about money is a sharper objection than uncertainty about quality.

nodes.label: 6.7 Who Takes You (lineage instead of testimonials)
nodes.rationale: There are no Trip Kailash testimonials and we do not invent them or paste Trekmania's on, because those people did not travel with Trip Kailash and a reader who checks will feel misled. Lineage is the honest version of the same claim and answers what a nervous buyer actually asks: who rescues me at 4,600 metres, and will this company exist next year. Verifiable beats copied.

nodes.label: 6.8 Before You Go (the SEO surface)
nodes.rationale: What the empty guide CPT is for and the entire SEO surface: queries like 'Muktinath yatra best time' and 'Kailash permit requirements' outrank any package name in search volume and feed the package pages. Cards open with the buyers' own framing taken from the research.

nodes.label: 6.9 The FAQ
nodes.rationale: Rewritten from the research as the objections buyers actually raise, answered without softening: fraud, refunds and the exact point Tibet permit money stops being recoverable, altitude, elderly parents, Horse Year timing, faith, and who is with you if you get sick. Every answer is an operational promise, not copy, and must be checked against how the business runs before shipping.

nodes.label: 6.10 The Form
nodes.rationale: A real server-side handler, not a static-site compromise. Submissions go to TK_FORM_RECIPIENT defined in functions.php and overridable from wp-config.php, and the recipient is deliberately never read from the form itself. The health question is new because the altitude conversation goes better starting at enquiry than at 4,600 metres, and adult children booking for a parent are relieved to be asked.

nodes.label: 6.11 Footer
nodes.rationale: Night ground, four columns, and a legal line that links to the verification section rather than merely asserting numbers.

nodes.label: The IATA Licence Flag
nodes.rationale: The current footer states 'IATA License: TK92456'. IATA accreditation is for airline ticketing agents, which this business is not. On a site whose central trust argument is check our numbers, one number that does not check out destroys the rest of them.

nodes.label: Section 7: The Vector Layer Plan
nodes.rationale: Everything drawn by hand, all of it honouring reduced motion by showing final states and stopping drives.

nodes.label: The Parikrama Line (the signature)
nodes.rationale: One brass hairline, one continuous SVG path drawn by scroll from the first viewport to the last, bending around each section rather than through it, closing into a circle behind the temple gallery and resolving into the kora ring. Driven by stroke-dashoffset against scroll progress, delta-gated so converged states cost nothing. Loudness test: remove it and the page becomes stacked sections instead of one walk.

nodes.label: The Brass Rule (section-heading ornament)
nodes.rationale: A hairline under each section heading with a small rotated square at its left end, echoing metal inlay on a temple door frame. Reframed as punctuation on the parikrama line: each rule is a segment of the same journey and the square is a step marker. One ornament, now with a reason.

nodes.label: The Fixed Environment Layer
nodes.rationale: One layer behind everything so scrolling feels like moving through a place rather than past stacked sections: radial brass bloom, vermilion and brass washes, feTurbulence paper grain at about 5%, background-attachment fixed so it never repaints on scroll.

nodes.label: Whisper Level, one per section
nodes.rationale: Slow four-second-plus cycles given negative animation delays so they are mid-cycle at first paint, paused off-screen by an IntersectionObserver class and on hidden tabs via body.paused. The selector reaches pseudo-elements explicitly because animation-play-state does not inherit.

nodes.label: The Twelve Laws, as a footage acceptance test
nodes.rationale: The laws predict which shots work before money moves; here they gate footage the operator already has. A clip failing law 1 (motion agrees with the scroll), 4 (plan the ending first) or 7 (compose for the layout) cannot be rescued by engineering. Inspection runs both directions: when the footage improves on the plan, the band map moves to feature it.

nodes.label: Section 8: The Engineering List
nodes.rationale: Named in full so the build cannot half-remember it; the underlying standard lives in 10k-websites/references/scrub-pipeline.md.

nodes.label: The Scrub Hero Engine
nodes.rationale: Fetch the video as a Blob behind an honest progress ring, because many hosts silently lack HTTP Range support and every seek then clamps to zero on the live site while working perfectly locally. Watchdog re-armed per chunk aborts to the still fallback rather than freezing the ring; the poster wins the bandwidth race by design; seeks are gated and coalesced with the busy flag reset on error so the gate cannot deadlock; the video is promoted to its own compositor layer.

nodes.label: Complete Without the Video
nodes.rationale: The page must be complete and beautiful if the video never loads, tested on purpose by renaming the file.

nodes.label: The Motion System
nodes.rationale: Nothing snaps; two easing tokens used everywhere. Entrances are choreography with .in added by IntersectionObserver and 60-150ms stagger, and stagger delays are retired after the entrance by a rule that matches or beats the nth-child specificity it retires. Only transform and opacity are animated, and JS never overwrites el.style.transition.

nodes.label: The Quality Floor
nodes.rationale: overflow-x clip with hidden first as fallback, reduced motion honoured in both directions, semantic landmarks with a skip link to #main, the scrub video aria-hidden and out of the tab order, :focus-visible in brass, 44px touch targets under coarse pointer, contrast computed rather than guessed, text sized in ch on the text element itself, and rows aligned on the baseline.

nodes.label: 8.1 Asset Processing (the scrub encode)
nodes.rationale: A keyframe every 8 frames is the difference between smooth and stuttering, so every scroll position seeks cleanly. Target 4-8 MB for a 6-second 1080p clip, step one variable at a time (crf then width) and judge by scrubbing. The ending-rest check is objective via frame differencing rather than a judgment call, and the ending frame is a free on-brand design asset to reuse in a lower section.

nodes.label: 8.2 WordPress Specifics
nodes.rationale: Video byte size passed to JS via wp_localize_script so the ring has a real total when Content-Length is missing; new style handles slot into the dependency-chained array in inc/enqueue.php which already solves the Elementor cascade-order problem; TRIP_KAILASH_VERSION and style.css Version move together or browsers keep old assets; LiteSpeed purged after every asset change; patch text with the editor tool, never a shell find-and-replace, which can read the UTF-8 file with the wrong encoding and turn every Devanagari character into mojibake.

nodes.label: 8.3 The Speed Receipts
nodes.rationale: Measured on the live URL after deploy, never estimated, because they are the proof that answers the standing objection to cinematic sites. Three numbers: page weight excluding the video, load time, and the video's size with its arrival time behind the ring, presented with the structural argument that heavy sections are theme templates rather than 90 KB of page-builder markup.

nodes.label: Section 9: The Copy Gate
nodes.rationale: A hard grep that must return zero for em dashes and the LLM tell words, then a sweep for quieter tells, run on every template because the drift lands in the lower sections. One carve-out: deliberate brand devices chosen in this package are craft, not tells, because a tell is what drifts in uninvited.

nodes.label: Section 10: Blockers Carried Into the Build
nodes.rationale: Ordered by urgency: whether a Kailash departure can still run before 30 September, the merit figure, the verification numbers, the IATA licence, real refund terms, every operational promise in the FAQ, a usable hero clip, the founder's name, and photography. Religious detail is worse wrong than absent, and the verification section cannot ship with placeholders.

nodes.label: Navbar and Footer Implementation Notes
nodes.rationale: Earlier implementation record for a transparent navbar integrated into the hero-video widget and a dark footer, written against the pre-redesign --tk-* palette.

nodes.label: Legacy --tk-* Palette (shiva, gold, bg-main)
nodes.rationale: --tk-shiva #1A1B3A dark navy, --tk-bg-main #F5F2ED light cream, --tk-gold #B8860B. The gold value survives into the redesign as --brass-500; the navy ground does not, being replaced by the warm night ramp.

nodes.label: Scroll-offset Navbar (50px threshold)
nodes.rationale: Navbar transparent at the top and darkened after scrolling 50px, integrated into the hero-video widget at z-index 5.

nodes.label: Footer Tagline: 'elevated by comfort'
nodes.rationale: 'Sacred luxury pilgrimages guided by devotion, elevated by comfort' is named by the design package's copy gate as a known hit for the tell word 'elevated'.

nodes.label: Footer Bottom Bar with IATA licence
header.php site header template
nodes.rationale: Transparent over a hero and solid past it, with the state decided by an IntersectionObserver rather than a scroll offset so it is correct whatever height the hero happens to be.

nodes.label: #tk-mobile-nav real mobile panel
nodes.rationale: A real element rather than a clone of the desktop nav, so the two cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: is-solid header state (IntersectionObserver on hero)
nodes.rationale: Watches .tk-hero or .tk-package-hero with rootMargin -72px so the change lands with the reader; a fixed scroll number would be wrong the moment the hero changes height.

nodes.label: 901px matchMedia panel guard
nodes.rationale: Widening past the breakpoint would otherwise leave the panel open and the body scroll-locked with no visible way to undo either.

nodes.label: Overlay renders legacy meta keys (trip_length, has_lodge, key_stops)
Overlay focus trap and focus restore
Class contract: .tk-rv/.tk-stagger -> .is-in/.is-done/.is-near
nodes.rationale: STAGGER_STEP 70ms and REVEAL_MS 700 must match motion.css by hand; the JS drives classes that the stylesheet styles.

nodes.label: scheduleDone: retire stagger delays after entrance
nodes.rationale: Without retiring the delays, every hover on the later siblings lags by its stagger for the life of the page.

nodes.label: Reduced motion handled in both directions
nodes.rationale: Turning it on pins every element to its final state and disarms the observers; turning it back off re-arms them instead of leaving pins behind. Re-arming one half is the half-fix that looks finished and is not.

nodes.label: bin/fetch-fonts.sh font vendoring script
nodes.rationale: Downloads Cinzel, Karla and Noto Serif Devanagari as variable woff2 into assets/fonts/, in latin, latin-ext (for the IAST diacritics) and devanagari subsets. Files are committed; the script is only re-run to update faces.

nodes.label: Dependency-chained stylesheet array
nodes.rationale: Registered individually rather than chained through @import, because @import makes the browser discover each file only after the previous one parses, producing a serial render-blocking waterfall. Separate handles download in parallel while the dependency chain preserves cascade order; fonts.css is first so @font-face parses before any rule asks for a face.

nodes.label: elementor-frontend dependency fix
nodes.rationale: Elementor prints frontend.min.css after every theme stylesheet, so the override file was losing every specificity tie on source order alone. Declaring the dependency lets WordPress order it correctly instead of escalating specificity forever, guarded on the handle existing because wp_enqueue_style silently drops a stylesheet with a missing dependency.

nodes.label: Front-page-only home.css, hero-scrub.js, parikrama.js, kora-ring.js, parikrama-line.js
nodes.rationale: Loaded after the Elementor overrides so the front page wins without escalating specificity, and conditionally because the pinned gallery and kora ring rules are dead weight on every other page. The scrub engine exits immediately unless the hero markup says a clip is configured.

nodes.label: Catalogue CSS on archive, taxonomies and Sacred Paths page
trip_kailash_preload_fonts() wp_head priority 1
nodes.rationale: A self-hosted font is only discovered after fonts.css downloads and parses, a full round trip late. Preloading only cinzel-latin.woff2 and karla-latin.woff2 removes the swap flash; the latin-ext and Devanagari subsets are unicode-range scoped and most pages never need them.

nodes.label: tk_package_field_schema()
nodes.rationale: One schema drives field registration, the admin UI, the REST shape and the templates, so nothing is defined twice and nothing can disagree with itself. Replaces specs typed into Elementor as layout text, which could not be filtered, sorted, compared or turned into schema and let the data drift (12 days in a title against 14 in a spec block).

nodes.label: tk_register_package_fields() on init
nodes.rationale: Native post meta rather than ACF, so the theme carries no plugin dependency; registered so REST and the block editor both see a predictable shape.

nodes.label: tk_package_field_rest_schema()
nodes.rationale: Repeaters and month lists need their item shape spelled out or WordPress refuses to expose them over REST at all.

nodes.label: tk_package() single field accessor
nodes.rationale: get_post_meta returns an empty string for an unset field, which prints as a blank spec row; this returns the schema default so an unfilled package degrades to something sensible rather than to a hole.

nodes.label: tk_package_has() render guard
nodes.rationale: A page printing 'Altitude: ' with nothing after it reads as broken, and an empty section reads as a hole to a first-time visitor.

nodes.label: tk_package_grading() label plus colour token
nodes.rationale: Returns the word and its var(--grade-*) token together, because a coloured dot alone tells a colour-blind reader nothing and grading is the field a buyer uses to decide whether they can go.

nodes.label: tk_package_overview() Elementor-guarded prose
nodes.rationale: An Elementor-built package returns nothing, because the_content() on one returns 88-120 KB of stored layout built for a page this template no longer renders. A missing section is recoverable; a page dumping a dead layout into the new design is not.

nodes.label: Departures field group (departure_type, fixed_departures, lead_time_note, best_months)
nodes.rationale: Fixed shows a date list, on-request shows a picker and the lead-time note. Real dates only: an invented departure date is the fastest way to lose a booking that was already yours.

nodes.label: Pricing field group (price_from, deposit_percent, group_pricing)
nodes.rationale: Always stored in USD with the site converting for display; deposit_percent defaults to 30, the share that holds a place with the balance due on arrival in Kathmandu.

nodes.label: Sitemap transient cache (TK_SITEMAP_CACHE_PREFIX, 6h TTL)
nodes.rationale: Sitemaps are rebuilt from unbounded queries over every published page, package, guide and lodge, and crawlers hit them often, so the finished XML is cached and rebuilt only when content changes or the cache expires.

nodes.label: Per-type sitemap builders (pages, packages, guides, lodges, deities)
Elementor widget tk-hero-video-v2
nodes.rationale: The video source is deliberately NOT rendered as a src attribute: autoplay makes the browser ignore preload hints and fetch the whole 27MB 4K file before first paint, over 90% of homepage weight on a phone over mobile data.

nodes.label: assets/js/video-controls.js (attaches the hero source)
nodes.rationale: Attaches the source only when the viewport is wide enough for the detail to matter and the visitor has not asked to save data; everyone else keeps the poster, the same first frame at a fraction of the bytes.

nodes.label: Elementor widget tk-sacred-paths-packages
nodes.rationale: Renders package cards with deity-taxonomy tab filtering; card specs are read with raw get_post_meta on the legacy keys rather than through the tk_package accessor.

nodes.label: Inline --tk-* token styles in legacy widgets
nodes.rationale: These widgets print their own <style> blocks using --tk-gold, --tk-bg-main, --tk-shadow-card and a 10px radius, which the redesign palette and its no-shadow rule supersede.

nodes.label: template-parts/home/departures.php
nodes.rationale: The date check lives in the template so the urgency band takes itself down rather than depending on someone remembering: a banner outliving its own deadline tells every returning visitor that nothing on the site is maintained.

nodes.label: template-parts/home/lineage.php
nodes.rationale: Every number comes from the Customizer and is omitted when unset, because a credential row showing dashes where figures belong advertises that nobody finished the page.

nodes.label: Lineage Customizer mods (years, travellers, guides, founder, portrait, reviews URL)
template-parts/package/inclusions.php
nodes.rationale: Inclusions and exclusions shown side by side with equal weight. A merged list, or exclusions buried below the fold, is where trust goes on a page asking for an international wire transfer; the exclusions column is the one a careful buyer reads first.

nodes.label: template-parts/package/reserve.php
nodes.rationale: Not a cart and never pretends to be one. Order is deliberate: pricing with group tiers first, then dates, then who is coming, then the money explainer and credentials, because doubt peaks right at the point of handing over details.

nodes.label: tk_website_url honeypot field
nodes.rationale: Reachable by a bot filling every field, out of the way of anyone using a keyboard or a screen reader.

tk_submit_contact_form AJAX handler
nodes.rationale: Reserve posts to the existing handler, which already carries the nonce, honeypot and rate limiting, rather than adding a second way in.

hyperedges.label: The hero delivery decision: scrub on desktop, designed still on phones
hyperedges.note: One shared flow: the same viewport/pointer/reduced-motion decision picks a Blob-fetched scrub video or a composed still, and it must be matched character for character across the CSS media queries, the JS gate, and the markup that withholds the video src.

hyperedges.label: The check-us-before-you-pay-us trust argument
hyperedges.note: The fraud pain, the invite-verification strategy, the named section, the FAQ answers, the lineage-instead-of-testimonials decision and the IATA blocker are one argument: every number on the site must be checkable, so one uncheckable number destroys the rest.

hyperedges.label: One field schema drives registration, REST, admin and every template
hyperedges.note: Adding a field means adding one row; nothing is defined in two places, so nothing can disagree with itself. Templates read only through tk_package/tk_package_has so unset fields degrade to schema defaults instead of blank spec rows.
